idea:what-the-state-pays-for-belongs-to-.title: No sovereignty without open source and open schemas; what the state pays for belongs to the commons; buy the alternative before the day you need it
idea:what-the-state-pays-for-belongs-to-.statement: Sovereignty means you can leave: a road with a toll gate owned by one company is lock-in with tarmac, and independence is the ability to run a parallel service, move the data and keep going, which exists only if the code and the schemas are open. What the public paid for should be available to the public, not so everyone changes the production system but so everyone can see it, run it and leave with their data, which is also how the local industry around it comes into being. And a market for the alternative does not appear on the day the single point of failure fails: run parallel services, buy the local or open alternative for part of the estate now and accept fewer features, and use procurement, the lever a state already holds, to prefer open schemas and data mobility.
idea:what-the-state-pays-for-belongs-to-.notes: The five-move playbook: map the attrition, commoditise the plumbing, create the demand, put the money where the market is genesis, regulate what settled, then map again. hack-your-country already cites sovereignty-is-the-ability-to-move for the test; this is the civic argument behind it, and the resilience case rather than an ideological one.

idea:smaller-models-more-of-them.title: Smaller models, more of them, with the least agency: a public model is a public road, and constraints are the input
idea:smaller-models-more-of-them.statement: Most work does not need a frontier model and should not use one: frontier models are for finding the art of the possible, and for things that have to work every day at a price they are too expensive, too much power for the task and dangerous in proportion; the right end state uses the model once to build the tool, and production is plain files and plain code with no prompt in the path, with agents given the least agency that does the job. The market still at genesis is small open models for each language and culture, the Portuguese of Portugal, Brazil, Angola, Cape Verde and Mozambique, not one Portuguese; Portugal released Amalia on 1 July 2026, built by a consortium of universities with 5.5 million euros of EU recovery money and published with its dataset and code under an open licence. Constraints are the input: DeepSeek's V3 was trained in 2.788 million GPU hours on export-restricted H800 chips, and the constraint produced the innovation.
idea:smaller-models-more-of-them.notes: 'The model is used once to build the tool, and production is plain files and plain code' is also a building principle for ship-now-ship-serverless and not-ready-to-be-in-line. The DeepSeek example is about constraint, not cost: the dollar figure is disputed and the article does not rely on it.

idea:millions-on-a-distributed-workforce.title: What spending millions on Upwork taught: build the infrastructure first, and the jobs can go back to where people came from
idea:millions-on-a-distributed-workforce.statement: As a CISO and CTO Dinis spent millions on Upwork across the open source projects and the teams he ran, and it was one of the most successful things they did: distributed teams, people as good as or better than those hired the ordinary way, delivered faster and more efficiently. It worked because they invested first in the infrastructure around it, a project management team, a structure team and an onboarding team, and then used Upwork to manage Upwork, so the internal teams carried no overhead. It was never buying the cheapest: it was the right talent at a price fair where they lived, good value for both sides and a real career for the person. A small country that builds the plumbing makes the jobs available everywhere inside it, so people can go back to where the family and the lifestyle are; Romania's technology sector is close to 8% of GDP with more than 250,000 professionals and over ten billion euros a year of service exports.
idea:millions-on-a-distributed-workforce.notes: The Upwork spend and outcomes are Dinis's own and not independently verifiable from the article. Answers the 2018 Upwork outline from the hiring side rather than the freelancer's.
